correctness.rationale: For each fixed odd p∤c, the polynomial symmetry Q_r(-n-1)=(-1)^r Q_r(n) makes v_n=c^n u_{p-1-n} obey the same recurrence as u_n on indices 1..p−2; recurrence at p−1 forces v_1=b u_{p−1}, while v_0=u_{p−1}. Invertibility of (n+1)^r for 1..p−2 permits induction to p−1, and Fermat c^{p−1}=1 gives e_p²=1. Coefficientwise reversal gives the polynomial identity; nonzero reciprocal roots pair, and Euler criterion gives factor cX²−1 when chi_p(c) differs from e_p. Checked endpoint p=3, negative c and c≠0, excluded p|c and nonintegral families; no general d≠0 cubic extension. Independently computed 4 integral families at odd primes through 59; finite tests support but do not prove the theorem.
